title: review-gate-matrix
description: Structured human-review-gate matrix produced by the human-review-gates skill. Maps a workflow's named gates to required reviewers, decision criteria, stop conditions, escalation, and documentation. Foundational primitive consumed by every output-builder skill in the repo (the sign-off block on a model card, issue write-up, vendor-diligence pack, SAR narrative, etc., references gate_id from this matrix). Stable contract: additive changes only between minor versions; breaking changes ship as a versioned migration.

gate_matrix_id.description: Stable identifier for this gate matrix instance. Reused across revisions of the same matrix.

as_of_date.description: Date this revision of the matrix was authored.

engagement_id.description: Foreign key into scope.schema.json when the matrix was built under a formal scope.

workflow_in_scope.description: The workflow, artifact lifecycle, or decision the matrix covers (e.g., 'AI use-case lifecycle for tier-1 retail credit', 'critical-vendor onboarding lifecycle', 'issue lifecycle for second-line findings', 'SAR-filing decision'). Scope tight; program-level scopes produce matrices nobody can adopt.

scope_notes.description: Optional clarification of the scope boundary (sub-processes excluded, jurisdictions covered, line-of-business carve-outs).

primary_committee.description: The body that pass/fails the gates in this matrix. Named role or named committee (e.g., 'AI Governance Committee', 'Vendor Risk Committee', 'Issue Review Committee').

escalation_committee.description: Where a no-pass routes when escalation is invoked. Often the next governance tier (e.g., Operational Risk Committee escalating to Risk Committee of the Board).

dissent_path.description: How an individual reviewer's challenge gets recorded and adjudicated. The dissent path is a governance artifact under SR 11-7 effective challenge and OCC Heightened Standards three-lines-of-defense expectations.

board_oversight.description: If this matrix is in scope of board-level oversight (Heightened Standards, Reg YY risk committee, NAIC corporate governance, ORSA), name the board body and reporting cadence.

source_posture.description: public-only: only public regulatory sources informed the matrix. firm-policy-overlay: firm policies and committee charters augment the public source set. mixed: both, with named seams.

label.description: Named source (e.g., 'SR 11-7 §VI', 'OCC Bulletin 2026-13', 'NIST AI RMF Govern function', 'firm AI Governance Policy v2.1 §3.4').

section_reference.description: Section, principle, or paragraph reference. Use [verify section] in references/source-anchors.md when the exact reference is not yet confirmed; do not invent section labels here.

gates.description: The matrix rows. Each gate is a named decision point in the workflow.

implied_gate_name.description: The gate that source guidance implies but the current workflow does not have (e.g., 'annual review gate for tier-1 AI use cases').

gap_description.description: What the gap is: gate not present, gate present but no independent reviewer, gate present but no stop conditions, gate present but no escalation path, gate present but documentation requirement is absent.

source_anchor.description: Path or label for the source that implies the gate (e.g., 'references/source-anchors.md#sr-11-7' or 'NIST AI RMF GV-4.1').

gate_gaps.description: Gates implied by source guidance but not present in the current workflow, or present but under-specified. A clean-looking matrix with no gaps usually means the gaps were buried.

recommended_charter_language.description: Suggested wording the committee charter or policy section can adopt directly. Reads as charter prose, not as matrix commentary. Optional; populated when the engagement is standing up or refreshing committee charter language.

narrative_summary.description: One-page narrative summarising the gate flow for committee adoption: decision authority, gate sequence, escalation, documentation. The narrative is the readable form for a board or committee that does not read matrices line by line.

owner_role.description: Named role (e.g., 'Head of Model Risk', 'Chief Compliance Officer'). Generic labels insufficient.

reviewer_questions.description: Questions for the human reviewer at sign-off. Tied to specific gates, gaps, or independence concerns; not generic ('is this fit for purpose').

confidence_label.description: Author's confidence in the matrix as a whole. Reflects source posture, completeness of the workflow inventory, and the quality of independence and stop-condition specification.

human_review_required.description: Always true. Gate architecture is committee-adopted; the skill stops at draft and the named reviewer attests.

revisions.description: Append-only revision log. Every material refresh of the matrix lands a row.

gate_id.description: Stable identifier for the gate. Foreign key for downstream artifact sign-off blocks (model-card, issue-writeup, vendor-diligence, SAR-narrative, etc.).

gate_name.description: Operational-language name (e.g., 'Tier-1 AI use-case go-live gate', 'Critical vendor pre-contract gate'). Names that read as slogans fail the namespace test.

stage.description: Where in the lifecycle the gate fires (intake, tiering, pre-prod, go-live, ongoing-monitoring, retirement; planning, due-diligence, contract, ongoing-monitoring, termination; identification, severity-rating, remediation, closure; etc.).

trigger.description: What brings a case to this gate. Event-based triggers name the event; periodic triggers name the cadence.

role.description: Named role (e.g., 'Head of Model Risk', 'Independent Validator', 'Chief Compliance Officer', 'CISO', 'Business Sponsor').

is_primary.description: True if this reviewer is the primary decision-holder for the gate.

is_backup.description: True if this reviewer is the named backup when the primary is unavailable.

independence_required.description: True when source guidance requires this reviewer to be independent of the artifact's producer or sponsor (SR 11-7 validation independence; interagency TPRM line-2; EU AI Act Article 14 competent oversight).

independence_basis.description: Source anchor or policy section that grounds the independence requirement (e.g., 'SR 11-7 §V', 'Interagency TPRM §III.D', 'firm AI Governance Policy v2.1 §4.2').

required_inputs.description: Artifact IDs that must be present at the gate (e.g., MODEL-CARD-XXX, VAL-REPORT-XXX, ISS-XXX, EV-XXX, EXIT-PLAN-XXX). A gate without named inputs is unauditable.

criterion.description: Declarative criterion (e.g., 'validation independence is established', 'no open critical or high issues against the model', 'exit plan exists and has been tested in the last 12 months').

source_anchor.description: Path into references/source-anchors.md, a loaded overlay file, or references/firm-overlay.md.

stop_conditions.description: Declarative, binary blockers (e.g., 'no go-live if any open critical issue', 'no contract if no exit plan'). 'Should be reviewed' is not a stop condition.

time_to_escalate.description: Cadence or window (e.g., 'within 5 business days', 'next scheduled committee').

escalation_owner.description: Named role that takes the case from the gate to the escalation forum.

documentation_requirement.description: What gets captured (decision, rationale, named attesters, date, artifact references, system of record). 'Minutes' acceptable when minute discipline names attesters and decisions; 'noted' is not.

frequency_detail.description: When frequency is event-based, name the event. When periodic, optionally name the calendar mechanism (e.g., 'Q3 risk committee meeting').

source_anchor.description: The named source for the gate's existence (e.g., 'SR 11-7 §VI', 'Interagency TPRM §III.B', 'EU AI Act Article 14', 'NIST AI RMF GV-4.1', 'firm AI Governance Policy v2.1 §3.4').

open_issue_ids.description: Foreign keys into the issue log for any current issues against this gate's design or operation.
